youtube_meta.title: I Leave My Worries at the Hive - A Gentle Surreal AI Music Film (4K)
youtube_meta.description:
I made this film as a soft whisper from the Hive — from nature, from the bees — for anyone who’s lived long enough to carry a few quiet burdens and still deserves a place to set them down. In this surreal Bee-Human world, the Hive isn’t just a hive… it’s a gentle sanctuary where time slows, dignity stays intact, and worry can finally rest. If the world has been moving too fast, I hope this feels like a warm chair by the window — a calm moment that honors what you’ve been through.

I Leave My Worries at the Hive is a gentle surreal AI music film created from 305 original images that I designed and shaped into one cohesive cinematic world, then brought to life in fluid motion to match the music. The songs are original and written by me, made to feel warm, timeless, and easy to return to — like a quiet place you can visit again.

🎵 Tracks on Bandcamp (Surreal AI)
00:00 — WHERE THE HONEY LEARNS TO BREATHE
04:08 — I LEAVE MY WORRIES AT THE HIVE

🎬 How it was made (original work, AI-assisted)
This film is an original creation directed and edited by me, using AI as a creative instrument:

Midjourney: crafted the original Bee-Human world visuals and concepts (305 images)

Veo 3: transformed still images into gentle cinematic motion (4K)

Suno: produced the original music from my lyrics and creative direction
AI was the tool — but the storytelling, pacing, visual choices, music writing, and final authorship are human-made.

top_comments.author: @karinandersson7949
top_comments.text:
Absolutely beautiful. And so true. Without the bees we would not only starve, we would be lost in space and time. They have senses we don't have. And if we respect them they will share that with us. 

Spacetime is more complex and convoluted than we humans, with our limited understanding of science, think. There are other ways of navigating through the multiverse. 

Also, in a very real sense, honey is liquid light. The bees make it from nectar that the flowers make from photosynthesis. From the sun. And if they are treated fairly, the bees are willing to share that with us. There is something fundamental in that. Something we should appreciate for what it is.
